newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian car sales soared in March -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Italian car sales soared in March -- newspaper.

text.p: Italian car sales soared in March to more than 220,000 units up from 176,321 in February, spurred by a government incentive scheme to kick-start the languishing industry, Milan business daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported.

The government launched a program of incentives at the beginning of the year under which owners of cars that have been on the road for more than 10 years receive a discount if they trade in their old car for a new one.
The newspaper said that March sales were particularly strong in view of the lower number of days worked as a result of the Easter weekend.
"The number of cars registered could have been higher if all the cars requested or sold had been immediately available," Il Sole reported.
Order portfolios had risen to unprecedented levels because of the shortage of available stock.

Renault had orders for 37,000 cars on its books after winning 22,000 new orders in March alone while orders for Fiat's subcompact models, such as the Panda and the Cinquecento, were running at double normal levels.
The Italian automobile association had struck off 138,976 old cars from the official car register since the launch of the government's incentive scheme on January 7.
